title: MLS Predictions: Last-Ditch Attempts at Postseason Places in Fateful Decision Day
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach Lowy12:00 PM ESTDecision Day will be full of intense duels. / Jeff Dean/MLS/Getty Images (top left); Griffin C. Hooper/Getty Images (bottom left); Geoff Stellfox/MLS/Getty Images (right)It all comes down to this. Saturday's regular season finale will feature 15 matches across a five-hour window, with vital implications for playoff seeding as well as playoff qualification.

There are a whopping six teams in the Western Conference that have yet to confirm if they will be competing in the 2026 MLS Cup playoffs or if they will be watching from their sofas. Meanwhile, in the East, there are a number of teams clawing for automatic playoff berths, desperate to avoid the wild card match.
Here, Sports Illustrated dives into how it all may play out.

Antoine Griezmann is seeking to continue his sensational run of form at Orlando. / Grant Halverson/MLS/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTThere’s bound to be goals galore in Orlando. Each of the last 11 meetings between the Lions and New England Revolution (including preseason) have featured at least three goals, with their two encounters this year producing 13 goals alone.

Whereas Orlando are looking to escape the wild card spots and sneak into an automatic berth, New England can surpass Inter Miami in second place with a win and a Miami defeat. Both teams have plenty to play for, making for a thrilling, high-scoring affair.
Score Prediction: Orlando City 3–4 New England Revolution

Cavan Sullivan will be looking to lead Philadelphia to a win on Saturday. / Jeff Dean/MLS/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTAfter a sensational run of form which saw them go 15 matches unbeaten and win eight in a row, Philadelphia Union have cooled off with just two points from their last four matches. Philadelphia have failed to score in each of their last two matches, and they'll be hoping to bounce back against Toronto FC.

Toronto's playoff dreams went up in smoke last weekend, with the Reds missing out on the postseason for a sixth straight year. As for Philadelphia, they know that a draw will be enough to see them avoid a wild card spot. A loss, however, could see them leapfrogged by Cincinnati and Columbus and dropped into eighth place. Don't be surprised if we see a third straight stalemate between these two.
Score Prediction: Philadelphia 2–2 Toronto

Miguel Almiron has been in red-hot form in the season's final weeks. / Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTAtlanta United said goodbye to their postseason ambitions on Oct. 28 after conceding a stoppage-time winner to New York City FC’s Bénie Traoré. Four days later, Red Bull New York's playoff ambitions came to a screeching halt after they squandered a 2–0 lead and conceded a stoppage-time goal to Nashville SC’s Sam Surridge.

The Red Bulls have collapsed in the final weeks with four losses in their last five, whereas Atlanta just ended a three-match losing streak with a 3–1 win against. Toronto. With Miguel Almirón in unstoppable form, expect Atlanta to close out the season with a victory.
Score Prediction: Red Bull New York 1–2 Atlanta United

Thomas Müller is seeking to lead Vancouver to victory in Montréal. / Geoff Stellfox/MLS/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTVancouver Whitecaps boast the second-best record in MLS, and they'll be traveling to the second-worst team in MLS: CF Montréal. Whereas the reigning MLS Cup finalists are heating up with three wins in their last four, the same cannot be said for their Canadian rivals, who have not won since Sep. 26.
While Vancouver are guaranteed first place in the West, they’ll nevertheless be looking to close out the regular season with a comprehensive victory in Montréal.
Score Prediction: CF Montréal 0–3 Vancouver Whitecaps

D.C. United are looking to close out 2026 with a win. / Kirk Irwin/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTIt has been a catastrophic second half of the season for New York City FC, who have won two of their last 15 MLS matches. NYCFC will miss the playoffs for just the third time in 12 years, and they'll be traveling to a D.C. United side that continues to be on the outside looking in on the postseason.

D.C. have lost five in a row but boast an impressive record against NYCFC, avoiding defeat in their last four meetings. They likely won’t be able to pick up a third straight win against the Boys in Blue, but they’re expected to end the season on a respectable note in front of home fans.
Score Prediction: D.C. United 0–0 New York City FC

Inter Miami are looking to wrap up second place. / Maddie Meyer/Getty ImagesDate: Saturday, Nov. 7Time: 4:00 p.m. ET / 1:00 p.m. PTTwo of the best teams in the East will go head to head in Florida as Inter Miami host Charlotte FC. Miami need to win to ensure that they finish second as opposed to third; Charlotte need a win (in addition to Chicago failing to win) in order to have hosting privileges for their first-round playoff series against Chicago.
